title: Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients

concept.text: The innovation would make a kidney recipient’s immune system durably accept a particular donor’s kidney while retaining protection against infections and other threats. The intended result is a healthy, functioning graft without ongoing maintenance systemic immunosuppression. Donor-specific tolerance means selective acceptance of the donor tissue; stopping medication alone does not establish that the recipient has preserved protective immunity.

The target is a predictable treatment across diverse donor–recipient combinations, with acceptable induction risks and durable benefit. The supplied clinical evidence demonstrates sustained medication withdrawal in selected, closely HLA-matched living-sibling recipients. That achievement supports the feasibility of the goal, but does not establish the broader capability. Safe induction, applicability beyond this selected population and preservation of protective immunity remain requirements of the proposed innovation.

significance.text: If broadly achieved, donor-specific tolerance could remove a central lifelong burden of kidney transplantation: maintaining enough systemic immunosuppression to protect the graft while managing the consequences of that treatment. Sustained withdrawal in the supplied trial provides a clinical basis for this possibility. A dependable approach could change transplantation from a continuing need to suppress immunity into a treatment that establishes lasting acceptance of the graft.

The magnitude of that benefit would depend on the safety of inducing tolerance and the recipient’s subsequent immune function. Freedom from maintenance medication would not eliminate all infection, malignancy or graft-loss risks. Claims of fewer serious infections, fewer cancers or better survival would require comparative outcome evidence; they do not follow automatically from successful drug withdrawal. The supplied abstract cannot establish those broader benefits.

Conditional downstream synthesis: a safe, durable approach could reduce medication-management burdens and make successful transplantation easier to sustain. Transfer to other transplanted organs would require organ-specific evidence. Application to autoimmune disease would require additional advances because accepting an external donor organ and correcting immune attack against the body’s own tissues are distinct problems.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unresolved capability in this record is reliable, durable tolerance across a substantially broader range of donor–recipient combinations. The documented trial studied adult recipients of kidneys from 2-haplotype HLA-matched living siblings. Its results do not determine whether the approach would work with greater immunologic mismatch or other donor circumstances, nor do they establish how long tolerance persists beyond the reported observation period. The supplied evidence also cannot establish the absence of broader methods throughout the field.

The demonstrated approach included non-myeloablative conditioning and infusion of a cellular product from the kidney donor. A broadly useful treatment must balance the ability to establish graft acceptance against the harms of conditioning and donor-cell treatment, including the need to avoid graft-versus-host disease. The abstract reports no graft-versus-host disease among treated recipients, but this small, selected cohort does not settle uncommon or longer-term risks. The supplied material does not justify characterizing the trial’s conditioning as dangerous.

Engineering and scientific synthesis: a dependable method would need to establish selective donor acceptance without broadly weakening protective immunity, identify recipients in whom medication withdrawal is appropriate, and detect failure early enough to protect the graft. It would also need a reproducible treatment process across centers. These are proposed requirements for making the capability predictable; the supplied abstract does not establish a validated solution to each one.

current_state.text: Kaufman and colleagues and the MDR-101-MLK Study Group reported a phase 3 multicenter randomized controlled trial in the American Journal of Transplantation in 2025. Adult recipients of kidneys from 2-haplotype HLA-matched living siblings were randomized 2:1: 20 to treatment and 10 to standard care. Treatment included non-myeloablative conditioning and infusion of the investigational donor-derived cellular product MDR-101.

The abstract reports that 19 of 20 treated recipients, or 95%, discontinued all immunosuppression approximately one year after kidney transplantation. Fifteen of 20, or 75%, reached the primary endpoint of more than two years without immunosuppression. Four resumed immunosuppression. These are distinct outcomes: initially stopping treatment and maintaining withdrawal for the specified interval. The abstract also reports no death, graft loss, donor-specific antibodies or graft-versus-host disease among treated recipients. These findings describe the reported cohort and follow-up, rather than establishing that such events cannot occur.

The evidence available for this record is a retained landing-page abstract, as described by the supplied review. Its extraction was untruncated, but the document remains partial evidence because full-text methods, detailed safety results and longer follow-up were unavailable in that retained copy. The supplied material does not provide sufficient control-arm outcome detail to quantify comparative benefits here. It also contains no verification record for the earlier claim of a publisher access error and no earlier pilot study with which to substantiate a direct comparison. The 2025 findings can be described at their stated date; the empty freshness record prevents a conclusion about the latest field-wide status.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: adequately powered multicenter studies would show sustained graft health after complete withdrawal of maintenance systemic immunosuppression, with enrollment extending beyond the closely matched living-sibling population. The documented trial’s withdrawal endpoint and standard-care comparison provide a starting point, but an endpoint of more than two years without medication should not by itself be treated as proof of lifelong tolerance.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained multicenter graft health after immunosuppression withdrawal beyond matched siblings

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: studies would compare rejection, graft function and survival, serious infections, malignancy, graft-versus-host disease and other treatment-related harms against standard care. They would explicitly assess protective immune responses, including responses to vaccination and clinically relevant infections, rather than infer preserved immunity solely from medication withdrawal. Adequate sample size, follow-up duration, acceptable event rates and definitions of graft health would need to be specified in advance; this record proposes no established numerical standard.
completion_criteria.label: Graft outcomes, harms, and protective immunity compared with standard care

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent centers would reproduce the results using a clearly specified treatment and withdrawal protocol, report recipients who fail to establish tolerance or need medication restarted, and define the donor and recipient groups for which the method has been demonstrated. Follow-up would assess delayed rejection and delayed treatment harms. Convincing finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those populations and conditions, rather than literal universality across every donor–recipient combination.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication with specified protocols and reported applicability limits

related_concepts.text: Roster synthesis: NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells,” and NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” address organ supply. NEP-07 addresses immune acceptance of a donor kidney. A manufactured kidney might still require an immune-compatibility strategy, depending on its cellular origin. Animal-donor kidneys pose additional compatibility questions; the supplied human HLA-matched sibling trial does not demonstrate tolerance to them. These concepts could complement one another while remaining separate capabilities.

Roster synthesis: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” and NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” seek restoration within the recipient’s existing kidneys. NEP-04, “A durable, implantable artificial kidney,” and NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” pursue replacement function through devices or delivery systems. NEP-07 instead seeks durable immune acceptance of a biological transplant; it neither regenerates nephrons nor supplies an artificial filtration system.

Roster synthesis: NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease,” and NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” address causes of native-kidney damage. Success could reduce the need for transplantation in affected populations. NEP-07 could improve transplantation for patients who still require it, but donor-specific tolerance would not itself establish correction of ADPKD, reversal of diabetic kidney disease or broad prevention of acute kidney injury.

unresolved_issues: The supplied freshness record is empty, so the latest field-wide availability of broader tolerance methods remains unassessed.
Applicability beyond adult recipients of 2-haplotype HLA-matched living-sibling kidneys and durability beyond the reported follow-up remain unresolved.
The retained abstract does not establish preserved protective immunity or quantify comparative reductions in infections, malignancy or mortality.
Full-text methods, detailed control-arm and safety outcomes, and explanations for medication resumption are not available in the supplied review.
The earlier pilot comparison and publisher access-error assertion cannot be verified from the supplied materials.
Proposed completion criteria still require protocol-specific definitions of adequate power, long-term follow-up, acceptable induction risks and sustained graft health.

brief.title: Lasting kidney acceptance without lifelong drugs
possible: People receiving a donated kidney could keep it healthy without lifelong drugs that suppress their immune system. Their body would accept that donor’s kidney while still defending against infections and other threats.
why: Kidney recipients would gain freedom from the continuing burden of managing drugs to prevent rejection. A dependable treatment could establish lasting acceptance of the kidney instead of requiring ongoing suppression of immunity.

sources.showed: A randomized trial used donor cells to help closely matched sibling kidney recipients stop immune-suppressing drugs. Most sustained withdrawal, although some restarted treatment.
sources.quote: demonstrated improved quality of life compared to standard treatment.
sources.cited_for: The trial supports the feasibility of sustained drug withdrawal in closely matched sibling recipients.
sources.not_established: It does not establish reliable acceptance with less closely matched donors or preserved protection against infections.

sources.showed: A small living-donor study reported years without rejection after withdrawal of immunosuppression (IS), drugs that suppress immunity. Researchers also assessed vaccine responses.
sources.quote:
All patients off IS continue to exhibit preserved kidney 
function, normal kidney allo- graft biopsies, and no donor-
specific antibodies.
sources.cited_for: Selected recipients can maintain healthy transplanted kidneys for years after stopping immune-suppressing drugs.
sources.not_established: This study does not establish predictable success across donor groups or comprehensive protection against infections.

sources.who: Stephan Busque and colleagues at Stanford University
sources.showed: Fully matched recipients achieved complete drug withdrawal with mixed chimerism, the continued presence of donor and recipient blood-forming cells. Less closely matched recipients encountered rejection during withdrawal.
sources.quote: Withdrawal of tacrolimus during the second year resulted in loss of detectable chimerism and subsequent rejection episodes, unless tacrolimus therapy was reinstituted.
sources.cited_for: The results show both successful withdrawal and the difficulty of extending it to less closely matched recipients.
sources.not_established: The approach did not reliably sustain complete drug withdrawal in less closely matched recipients.

shown: In Kaufman and colleagues’ randomized trial, 75% of treated recipients achieved sustained freedom from immune-suppressing drugs. All received kidneys from closely matched living siblings.
Leventhal and colleagues reported that 26 living-donor recipients stopped these drugs without rejection and maintained healthy kidneys for years.
missing: Reliable, lasting kidney acceptance still needs demonstration across a much broader range of donors and recipients.
The treatment must preserve protection against infections while keeping the donated kidney healthy.
Larger, longer studies must establish treatment safety and ways to identify when withdrawal is appropriate or failing.

milestones.label: Healthy kidneys after drug withdrawal beyond closely matched siblings
milestones.explanation: Studies across multiple centers would have to show sustained kidney health after complete drug withdrawal beyond closely matched sibling recipients. This would establish broader usefulness.

milestones.label: Kidney health, treatment safety and immune protection compared
milestones.explanation: Studies would compare rejection, kidney function and survival, infections, cancer, treatment harms and immune responses with standard care. This would test whether drug freedom preserves health and protective immunity.

milestones.label: Independent success with clear treatment rules and limits
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would reproduce results using specified protocols and report failures, restarts, eligible groups and delayed harms. This would establish reproducibility and the treatment’s demonstrated limits.

uncertain: How long acceptance lasts beyond the observed follow-up remains unresolved.
Acceptable treatment risks, follow-up length and definitions of sustained kidney health still need clear thresholds.

page.title: Donor-specific tolerance induction in kidney transplantation
page.definition: A treatment enables a recipient to keep a functioning donor kidney without long-term anti-rejection drugs while retaining immune responses to unrelated antigens. Drug-free graft function is called operational tolerance and can coexist with measurable immune reactivity to the donor. Evidence applies to the donor–recipient group studied. For example, the MDR-101 randomized trial enrolled adults whose living sibling donor matched both inherited sets of human leukocyte antigens (HLA), the proteins used for tissue matching.

goal.need: The United States recorded 27,351 adult kidney transplants in 2023. Recipients generally need lifelong anti-rejection drugs that increase the risk of serious infection and cancer. Simply stopping the drugs can trigger rejection. Durable tolerance would spare recipients the continuing side effects of treatment while protecting the kidney. The benefit depends on safe induction: donor-cell therapy can itself cause graft-versus-host disease, in which donor immune cells attack the recipient.

completion.title: FDA licenses a biological treatment for inducing kidney transplant tolerance without maintenance drugs.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics license for an indication permitting complete withdrawal of maintenance immunosuppression after kidney transplantation. For the donor–recipient population covered by the indication, clinical assessment, laboratory tests and graft histology show normal or stable kidney function off maintenance treatment, and immune testing demonstrates responses to non-donor antigens.
completion.set_by: FDA sets the biologics licensing requirements in 21 CFR 601.2 and 601.4. The Immune Tolerance Network defines the clinical and immunological components of transplant tolerance.
completion.threshold_quote: that the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements established in this chapter.
completion.basis: Licensure establishes the approved use for the specified population. The clinical evidence of donor specificity follows the ITN strategic plan. The MDR-101 sponsor reported completion of the registration trial and subsequently sought an acquirer to complete the license application. Neither MDR-101 nor FCR001 appears on FDA’s licensed cellular and gene therapy product list.

milestones.title: An animal kidney recipient accepts donor tissue and rejects unrelated donor tissue without maintenance drugs.
milestones.criterion: An animal with a functioning kidney transplant and no maintenance immunosuppression accepts a second graft from the kidney donor and rejects a graft from a third-party donor.
milestones.set_by: Experimental transplantation’s donor-versus-third-party graft challenge, applied in dogs and nonhuman primates. Human HLA matching categories do not apply to the animal test.
milestones.threshold_quote: a second graft from the same donor should be accepted, whereas a graft from a third-party donor should be rejected.

milestones.title: After tolerance induction, a kidney recipient maintains graft function for at least one year off drugs.
milestones.criterion: After a tolerance-directed intervention and complete withdrawal of immunosuppression, a kidney transplant recipient maintains stable graft function for at least one year without immunosuppressive drugs. The interval starts when the last immunosuppressive drug is stopped. This clinical observation establishes operational tolerance over that interval.
milestones.set_by: Clinical transplantation's operational-tolerance convention, documented by Massart and colleagues. Definitions of satisfactory graft function differ between studies; the 1-year minimum is shared.
milestones.threshold_quote: All authors agreed upon a strict minimal period of 1 year without immunosuppression before evoking tolerance.

milestones.title: A drug-free kidney recipient has a postvaccination antibody titre greater than twice the baseline titre.
milestones.criterion: In a kidney recipient off immunosuppression, divide the antibody titre after vaccination by the titre before vaccination for the same antigen. A ratio greater than 2 meets the FCR001 study’s protective-response category for tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis or a tested pneumococcal serotype. This measures a response to the tested antigen.
milestones.set_by: Leventhal and colleagues, published FCR001 phase 2 immunocompetence assessment in living-donor kidney recipients. Chimerism means the presence of donor-derived blood cells; this assay threshold was not established separately for deceased-donor recipients.

milestones.title: At least 48% of MDR-101 recipients meet the 24-month drug-free tolerance endpoint.
milestones.criterion: In the randomized phase 3 trial of HLA-matched living-donor kidney transplantation, at least 48% of recipients assigned to MDR-101 must reach functional tolerance. After qualifying for withdrawal, a recipient stops all immunosuppression by about month 12 and remains off it for at least 24 additional months, through month 36, without biopsy-proven acute rejection, new donor-specific antibodies, graft-versus-host disease, kidney graft loss or death. Loss to follow-up counts as failure in the intention-to-treat analysis.
milestones.set_by: Medeor Therapeutics, MDR-101-MLK protocol NCT03363945. The investigators specified the treatment-arm target for this trial.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least 48% IA-R IS-Free for at least 24 mos

milestones.title: An MDR-101 recipient reaches 5% donor blood-cell chimerism and qualifies for tacrolimus withdrawal.
milestones.criterion: In the MDR-101 matched living-donor protocol, assess eligibility to taper tacrolimus at about six months after kidney transplantation. Donor-derived cells must account for at least 5% of blood-forming cells, with no biopsy-proven acute rejection, graft-versus-host disease or kidney graft loss. This threshold applies to withdrawal under this protocol.
milestones.set_by: Medeor Therapeutics, MDR-101-MLK protocol NCT03363945, as specified by the trial investigators.
milestones.threshold_quote: if donor hematopoietic mixed chimerism was ≥5%, and no rejection (BPAR), GvHD, or kidney loss.

milestones.title: The sponsor submits a biologics license application for kidney transplant tolerance to FDA.
milestones.criterion: After the pivotal trial, the sponsor submits a biologics license application to FDA for the treatment and the proposed kidney transplant indication. The application includes nonclinical and clinical data supporting the product’s safety, purity and potency.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 601.2(a). The CIRM public review of MDR-101 identifies application submission as the project objective following phase 3.
milestones.threshold_quote: the manufacturer shall submit an application to the Director

not_found: No field-wide numerical success-rate, induction-risk or durability threshold spanning all donor–recipient groups was found in the ITN plans or EMA concept paper.

results.finding: 19 of 20 MDR-101 recipients stopped all immunosuppression under a chimerism-gated tacrolimus withdrawal protocol.
results.detail: The count is for completed withdrawal. The abstract gives no separate count of recipients who met all eligibility conditions at approximately six months.
results.quote: Nineteen (95%) successfully discontinued all immunosuppression approximately 1-year post-kidney transplant.

results.finding: 15 of 20 MDR-101 recipients maintained graft function off all immunosuppression for more than two years.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study end-point of immunosuppression-free for > 2 years.

results.finding: 75% of the 20 recipients assigned to MDR-101 reached the primary endpoint of more than two years off immunosuppression.
results.detail: Four recipients resumed immunosuppression, and one did not complete withdrawal.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study end-point of immunosuppression-free for > 2 years.

results.finding: Among 37 FCR001 living-donor kidney recipients, 26 maintained graft function for at least one year off immunosuppression.
results.detail: The counts and durations are for the full FCR001 cohort. The supplied text gives no HLA-stratified counts or durations.
results.quote:
Twenty-six patients were successfully 
taken off IS (time   off   IS   36–123 mo) without rejection.

results.finding: Seven drug-free FCR001 kidney recipients were assessed after Pneumovax and showed protective antibody responses with titre ratios >2.
results.detail: The supplied text reports the vaccine responses by chimerism group and gives no HLA breakdown for the seven recipients.
results.quote:
Likewise, patients demonstrated higher pro- F5 
tective response rates in 12 of 14 serotypes following 
Pneumovax (Figure 6).

results.finding: Among 29 fully HLA-matched living-donor kidney recipients, those who stopped all immunosuppression had a median of 48 months off drugs.
results.detail: The 48-month median applies to the 24 recipients who stopped all immunosuppression. The study reports later resumption of immunosuppression in some recipients.

results.finding: Among 22 HLA-mismatched living-donor kidney recipients, zero achieved documented one-year drug-free graft function.
results.detail: Tacrolimus tapering or withdrawal was associated with loss of detectable chimerism and, in some recipients, rejection.
results.quote: Patient no. 2 lost chimerism shortly after discontinuation of tacrolimus and developed a biopsy-proven rejection episode 3 months later.

results.finding: In the 29-recipient HLA-matched living-donor cohort, 24 proceeded to withdrawal under the study’s chimerism-based rules.
results.detail: Recipients tapered cyclosporine or tacrolimus. The paper’s 5% engraftment definition applied to dose escalation in the haplotype-matched cohort.
results.quote: Twenty-four of 29 fully HLA-matched recipients were completely withdrawn from IS drugs after mixed chimerism persisted for at least 6 months.

results.finding: Of 29 HLA-matched living-donor kidney recipients in the phase 1/2 study, 19 had at least 24 months off immunosuppression.
results.detail: The count comes from individual durations in Table 1. Complete withdrawal occurred between months 6 and 18, so 24 months off drugs is insufficient to establish the prespecified month-36 endpoint.

results.finding: 25 of 32 HLA-mismatched living-donor kidney recipients fully withdrew immunosuppression after tolerance induction.
results.detail: The reported one-year time point marks when tacrolimus was stopped. The milestone’s one-year observation period starts at that point.
results.quote: Of the 32 patients, 26 developed high-level donor or mixed stable chimerism, followed by complete withdrawal of immunosuppression (IS) in 25 patients.

results.finding: One deceased-donor kidney recipient maintained good graft function for at least 12 years off immunosuppression.
results.detail: A mixed leukocyte reaction showed vigorous reactivity to donor cells despite sustained drug-free graft function.
results.quote: Operational tolerance to HLA-A, B, and DR mismatched organ allografts can be induced prospectively in humans for at least 12 years after withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs.

results.finding: Five HLA-mismatched living-donor kidney recipients maintained graft function for more than 2.5 years after complete immunosuppression withdrawal.
results.detail: The study selected five recipients with sustained drug-free graft function. Three other recipients who initially achieved tolerance and later resumed immunosuppression were excluded from the comparison.
results.quote:
The tolerant group con-
sisted of 5 patients who successfully achieved long-term (>13, >6.9, >6.7, >6.4, and >2.5 years) immunosup-
pression-free allograft survival after HLA haplotype-matched CKBMT.

results.finding: The initial recipient in a 10-patient HLA-matched sibling transplant series maintained normal graft function for nearly 20 years off immunosuppression.
results.detail: Cyclosporine was discontinued on post-transplant day 73.
results.quote:
After receiving no immunosuppressive therapy for nearly
20 years, renal allograft function has remained normal.

Donors were

results.detail: The paper reports 23 known HLA mismatches and 21 deceased donors among the 35 recipients, so at least two mismatches involved living donors. It gives no joint count for donor type and HLA match status.

The remaining 23 patients had a mean number of

definition = "A treatment enables a recipient to keep a functioning donor kidney without long-term anti-rejection drugs while retaining immune responses to unrelated antigens. Drug-free graft function is called operational tolerance and can coexist with measurable immune reactivity to the donor. Evidence applies to the donor\u2013recipient group studied. For example, the MDR-101 randomized trial enrolled adults whose living sibling donor matched both inherited sets of human leukocyte antigens (HLA), the proteins used for tissue matching.". Reason: The definition replaces an unspecified reference to populations with a concrete trial population and explains why drug-free graft function alone gives incomplete evidence of specificity.

goal.need = "The United States recorded 27,351 adult kidney transplants in 2023. Recipients generally need lifelong anti-rejection drugs that increase the risk of serious infection and cancer. Simply stopping the drugs can trigger rejection. Durable tolerance would spare recipients the continuing side effects of treatment while protecting the kidney. The benefit depends on safe induction: donor-cell therapy can itself cause graft-versus-host disease, in which donor immune cells attack the recipient.". Reason: The current rationale points to absent regimen data and omits the harms of lifelong treatment, the consequence of simply stopping it and the risks of induction.

add statement by California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, Grants Working Group, 2017: "Demonstrate the ability to achieve durable immune tolerance.". Reason: The CIRM review identifies a public programme with a kidney-specific development objective for HLA-matched living-donor recipients.

edit completion: criterion = "FDA issues a biologics license for an indication permitting complete withdrawal of maintenance immunosuppression after kidney transplantation. For the donor\u2013recipient population covered by the indication, clinical assessment, laboratory tests and graft histology show normal or stable kidney function off maintenance treatment, and immune testing demonstrates responses to non-donor antigens."; set_by = "FDA sets the biologics licensing requirements in 21 CFR 601.2 and 601.4. The Immune Tolerance Network defines the clinical and immunological components of transplant tolerance."; threshold_quote = "that the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements established in this chapter."; threshold_ref = 5; basis = "Licensure establishes the approved use for the specified population. The clinical evidence of donor specificity follows the ITN strategic plan. The MDR-101 sponsor reported completion of the registration trial and subsequently sought an acquirer to complete the license application. Neither MDR-101 nor FCR001 appears on FDA\u2019s licensed cellular and gene therapy product list."; refs = [5, 2, 6, 19]. Reason: The revision identifies the evidence required by the ITN definition and distinguishes the sponsor’s phase 3 result from FDA’s licensing decision.

edit m1: criterion = "An animal with a functioning kidney transplant and no maintenance immunosuppression accepts a second graft from the kidney donor and rejects a graft from a third-party donor."; set_by = "Experimental transplantation\u2019s donor-versus-third-party graft challenge, applied in dogs and nonhuman primates. Human HLA matching categories do not apply to the animal test."; threshold_quote = "a second graft from the same donor should be accepted, whereas a graft from a third-party donor should be rejected."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 20, 8]. Reason: The animal criterion currently includes one monkey’s results and omits earlier canine evidence for the same donor-versus-third-party challenge.

add milestone after m1: "An MDR-101 recipient reaches 5% donor blood-cell chimerism and qualifies for tacrolimus withdrawal.". Reason: MDR-101 has a prespecified safety decision before drug withdrawal that can be assessed before a recipient accrues drug-free follow-up.

edit m2: title = "After tolerance induction, a kidney recipient maintains graft function for at least one year off drugs."; criterion = "After a tolerance-directed intervention and complete withdrawal of immunosuppression, a kidney transplant recipient maintains stable graft function for at least one year without immunosuppressive drugs. The interval starts when the last immunosuppressive drug is stopped. This clinical observation establishes operational tolerance over that interval."; threshold_quote = "All authors agreed upon a strict minimal period of 1 year without immunosuppression before evoking tolerance."; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9, 10, 11, 14]. Reason: The criterion now measures a year from complete drug withdrawal after a tolerance-directed intervention and removes cohort results from the test.

edit m3: title = "A drug-free kidney recipient has a postvaccination antibody titre greater than twice the baseline titre."; criterion = "In a kidney recipient off immunosuppression, divide the antibody titre after vaccination by the titre before vaccination for the same antigen. A ratio greater than 2 meets the FCR001 study\u2019s protective-response category for tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis or a tested pneumococcal serotype. This measures a response to the tested antigen."; threshold_quote = "a ratio of >2 as \u201cprotective response.\u201d"; threshold_ref = 11. Reason: The vaccine criterion now gives the paired measurement and its assay-specific interpretation without including serotype or cohort results.

edit m4: title = "At least 48% of MDR-101 recipients meet the 24-month drug-free tolerance endpoint."; criterion = "In the randomized phase 3 trial of HLA-matched living-donor kidney transplantation, at least 48% of recipients assigned to MDR-101 must reach functional tolerance. After qualifying for withdrawal, a recipient stops all immunosuppression by about month 12 and remains off it for at least 24 additional months, through month 36, without biopsy-proven acute rejection, new donor-specific antibodies, graft-versus-host disease, kidney graft loss or death. Loss to follow-up counts as failure in the intention-to-treat analysis."; set_by = "Medeor Therapeutics, MDR-101-MLK protocol NCT03363945. The investigators specified the treatment-arm target for this trial."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "at least 48% IA-R IS-Free for at least 24 mos"; threshold_ref = 21; refs = [21, 22, 12]. Reason: The current milestone substitutes an individual duration for the trial’s prespecified treatment-arm target and omits the clinical events that disqualify a response.

add milestone after m4: "The sponsor submits a biologics license application for kidney transplant tolerance to FDA.". Reason: Submission of the biologics license application is an explicit project objective between completion of the pivotal trial and FDA licensure.
